basics.name: Andrew McLoughlin
basics.label: Full-stack developer of scientific software / Data Engineer / Statistician

summary: Full-stack developer of scientific software[cite: 1] with an academic foundation in computational biology and epidemiology[cite: 1] (MPhil from Cambridge[cite: 3], MSc/BSc from Warwick[cite: 3]). Over a decade of experience across healthcare-related start-ups[cite: 10] specializing in building robust data pipelines, analytics applications, clinical data systems[cite: 1], and public-facing scientific databases (such as the Gates Foundation-funded VOC Atlas)[cite: 2]. Combines technical production-grade expertise in Python, Django, PostgreSQL, and dbt with deep knowledge of clinical data management, compliance (GDPR, GCP, 21 CFR Part 11, CDISC/CDASH)[cite: 2], and product ownership[cite: 2].

work.name: Owlstone Medical
highlights: Product Owner and lead developer for www.vocatlas.com, a greenfield public-facing Django application helping scientists identify compounds on breath across populations, funded in part by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation[cite: 1, 2, 4, 5].

Managed cross-functional teams (scientists, designers, developers, QC, marketing), maintaining Jira backlogs, tracking OKRs, defining user personas, and leading stakeholder meetings with the Gates Foundation[cite: 2, 5].

Designed and deployed a lightweight internal order fulfillment management application with interactive analytics dashboards integrated with Royal Mail shipping API, reducing data entry error rates from 5% to negligible levels and completely obsolescing a 2-hour weekly meeting[cite: 1, 5].

Set up the company Data Team to tackle inefficient/non-compliant data practices and championed the adoption of a single company-wide open-source Data Warehouse (using Airbyte, Airflow, dbt, PostgreSQL, and SQL) following Kimball's toolkit best practices[cite: 1, 2, 8].

Built and automated ETL pipelines ingesting millions of rows of GCMS data, connecting third-party APIs, and feeding interactive business intelligence dashboards used by hundreds of employees to drive key leadership decisions[cite: 1, 2].
Led UX/UI design of the OMED mobile app and website, building interactive prototypes in Figma and Penpot to quickly iterate on user feedback[cite: 6, 7].

Maintained a monolithic Django-based Laboratory Management Information System (LIMS) used daily by over 200 employees with 100% uptime over 8 years, utilizing Kubernetes, Docker/containers, PostgreSQL, Gitlab CI/CD, Pytest, and Sentry[cite: 6, 7].
Ensured rigorous data governance, security, and compliance with GDPR, GCP, and 21 CFR Part 11 via automated immutable audit logging, SSO, and MFA minimal access controls[cite: 2].
Productionised statisticians' research code into tested, version-controlled Python packages with strict automated testing and 100% code coverage[cite: 1, 2].

work.name: Owlstone Medical
highlights: Managed clinical trial data (such as the LuCID clinical trial, a large-scale prospective case-control study evaluating breath-based biomarkers for lung cancer over a 24-month follow-up across 26 clinical sites in 5 countries)[cite: 2].
Applied Multivariate Pattern Recognition and Classification Algorithms in Python to differentiate signals between cases and controls, presenting insights via PowerBI[cite: 2].
Designed CDISC/CDASH-compatible Case Report Forms (CRFs) using SNOMED-CT and MedDRA clinical terminologies, preparing datasets for FDA submission and cross-study aggregation[cite: 1, 2].

work.name: Optimum Patient Care (Research in Real Life)
highlights: Designed and built CRFs in OpenClinica, enforcing robust data quality with edit checks, skip logic, and comprehensive documentation[cite: 2, 3].
Built interactive dashboards to report study recruitment metrics and endpoints to study managers, enabling early identification and resolution of demographic imbalances across study arms[cite: 2, 3].
Ingested and processed complex real-world data into OPCRD, executing data validation and cleaning scripts[cite: 2, 3].
Transitioned clinical teams from paper-based operations to fast, efficient, and compliant digital systems across the EU, UK, and US for over 10 clinical trials[cite: 6, 7].

projects.name: VOC Atlas (www.vocatlas.com)
projects.description: A public-access breathomics database and educational web application built with Django to help scientists identify volatile organic compounds on breath across populations.
highlights: Served as Product Owner and Lead Developer, taking the project from ideation and Figma low-fi mockups to full deployment, user testing, and population[cite: 1, 4, 5].
Involved complex chemical data modeling, user interviews, shadowing, analytics tracking, and stakeholder management with the Gates Foundation[cite: 1, 4, 5].

projects.name: Enterprise Data Warehouse & ETL Pipelines
projects.description: Company-wide data architecture replacing fragmented reporting with open-source infrastructure.
highlights: Designed and built automated ETL pipelines and an open-source Data Warehouse following Kimball's best practices, extracting sensitive medical data and loading it into interactive BI dashboards[cite: 1, 6, 7].
Integrated automated data quality testing and monitoring to notify teams of QC issues[cite: 1].

projects.name: Internal Order Fulfillment & Logistics Application
projects.description: Lightweight operations management app replacing manual spreadsheets.
highlights: Prototyped in Figma after shadowing operations teams, built with Django, and integrated with the Royal Mail shipping API[cite: 1, 5].
Provided live KPI dashboards and an immutable audit trail, reducing data entry errors from 5% to effectively zero[cite: 1, 5].

projects.name: Smart Watch Actimetry Algorithm (MSc Thesis)
projects.description: Researched and developed signal processing algorithms to train machine learning models identifying physical activities from raw actimetry data collected via open-source smartwatch prototypes[cite: 6, 7].

projects.name: Metabolism Browser (BSc Thesis)
projects.description: Interactive software teaching aid built in Visual Basic designed to help students explore and visualize complex metabolic pathways[cite: 6, 7].
